title: POC throughput standup - queue shaping & batch profiling
summary: Weekly POC standup to review throughput numbers from the last 48h, align on new concurrency targets, test queue-shaping config, and agree next steps for a focused retune. Decided to raise target concurrency for the 1k qps path after adjusting batch cutoffs and to run a controlled stress with burst capacity enabled.
action_items: Liam - produce batch-size distribution chart and attach to the pilot sheet by 2026-11-02
Tom - run KV cache warmup script on staging and report p95 improvements by 2026-11-01
Maya - share updated pricing impact for increased concurrency scenario by 2026-11-03
next_steps: Schedule 90-min deep dive if stress run shows >10% regression
Run 30-min smoke with burst capacity + fallback enabled Tue morning (Redwood to confirm region)
Customer to provide 1000-sample prompt set for quality verification
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rachel (Head of Infra - Solstice), Tom (ML), Priya (SRE), Evan (Product)

[00:00] Maya: alright everyone good to go, thanks for hopping on for the weekly POC stand-up. we wanna focus on throughput tuning today, quick numbers first.
[00:12] Rachel: yep, go ahead. we ran the steady-state run overnight, results are in the sheet, uh I pulled p95 and p99, there's a weird tail around 800ms.
[00:22] Liam: okay let's call out the baseline - last baseline config was concurrency 8, batch cutoff 40 tokens, continuous batching enabled, no burst. average token throughput ok but the p99 spikes with rps bursts.
[00:35] Tom: i can confirm the p99 spikes tied to queueing, i saw queue depth climb on a few nodes then one of them hit backpressure and timed out a second or two.
[00:47] Priya: that aligns with what our SREs saw - the kube HPA scaled a bit slow and we got some queuing. not sure if the autoscaler is the main cause or the serving runtime batch behavior.
[01:05] Liam: couple things we tried locally - lowering batch cutoff to 20 tokens reduced p99 by ~18% under constant load but throughput dropped slightly. continuous batching heuristics need a different threshold for this prompt distribution.
[01:25] Evan: question: does lowering cutoff mean more small batches -> more cost?
[01:28] Maya: yes, in general smaller batches increase per-token compute overhead, cost up. but we can offset by bumping concurrency and enabling KV cache to reduce repeated work.
[01:40] Rachel: what's the tradeoff window we should test?
[01:42] Liam: propose 3 arms: 1) raise concurrency to 12 with cutoff 40, 2) keep concurrency 8 but cutoff 20 + batch warmup, 3) concurrency 10 with adaptive cutoff (auto step-down on latency). we'll run each for 1 hour in staging under the same synthetic trace.
[02:05] Tom: for the synthetic trace can we use the 1k qps ramp profile? last time we used it it exposed the tails.
[02:12] Liam: yes use the 1k qps ramp. also enable KV cache warmup prior to starting the run so we don't penalize cold paths.
[02:20] Priya: how do we warm the KV cache? script or traffic replay?
[02:23] Tom: traffic replay with a shorter TTL on cache entries and a targeted script that primes the top 100 prompt prefixes. i'll run that.
[02:30] Maya: ok action - Tom will run warmup, Liam will attach batch distribution chart, Maya will model pricing delta for concurrency changes.
[02:38] Rachel: quick note on networking - if we enable burst capacity, we'll want to confirm subnet egress rules and expected region fallback; last time packets were routed to us-east-2 and latency jumped.
[02:52] Liam: we can pin region for the test, we'll confirm which infra pool the burst capacity uses. we'll also test fallback to a smaller quantized model if main pool saturates.
[03:05] Evan: what's the expected change to quality if fallback model used?
[03:09] Liam: there's a small drop in perplexity, for our eval set it was about 2-3% quality delta. we should run the 1000 prompt quality pass after throughput runs to verify there's no regression.
[03:22] Tom: yep I will run eval and post top 10 failure cases.
[03:26] Priya: one more operational ask - audit logs, we need to ensure request-level logs go to our SIEM for the burst test.
[03:32] Maya: that's in the security pack, i'll attach the SOC2 + audit-log integration doc.
[03:36] Rachel: perfect. also SSO question from our security team - they want confirmation SAML/SO works with private deployment; not urgent for this run but wanted to flag.
[03:45] Maya: noted, we'll route that to solution engineering follow-up.
[03:48] 
[04:02] (--- mid-call technical exchange, timestamps every ~60s now ---)
[04:02] Liam: looking at the raw traces, there's a pattern: when queue depth goes above 250 requests in flight, the percent of 1-token batches drops and latency climbs. continuous batching has an eviction timer set to 120ms right now.
[04:18] Tom: could we reduce the eviction timer to 80ms? might let more smaller batches form but also reduce latency in the tail.
[04:25] Liam: yes that is an option, but we need to test because reducing timer increases small batch prevalence -> cost. we can do a micro test with 10-minute window.
[04:40] Priya: our preference is p95 under 350ms, p99 under 700ms, those are our internal SLOs. current config met p95 but p99 was ~880ms.
[04:52] Liam: ok, aim to hit p99 <700ms. with adaptive cutoff + concurrency bump I think it's achievable.
[05:05] Rachel: how will we surface results? sheet plus a brief note in the pilot tracker?
[05:09] Maya: yes we'll update the pilot tracker row; Liam will paste batch hist and Tom will add eval notes.
[05:15] Evan: any thoughts on running a short canary to prod-like infra afterwards?
[05:18] Maya: we can run a canary in the dedicated pool but need procurement sign-off to enable burst in dedicated, otherwise we'll run in hosted but isolated VPC region.
[05:30] Tom: can we also test the quantized variant as a fallback? the perf is better but sometimes hallucination rates change.
[05:36] Liam: we'll set fallback thresholds: if queue wait > 120ms for 5s, route to q4 quantized variant for 30s then reassess. it's in the routing policy we can enable for test.
[05:50] Rachel: anything else on the telemetry side?
[05:52] Priya: please include per-token cost breakdown for each test arm. helps our finance lead decide.
[05:57] Maya: will include that.
[06:00] 
[06:10] (final 10 minutes - recap + scheduling)
[06:10] Maya: recap: run three arms (concurrency12/cutoff40, concurrency8/cutoff20 + warmup, concurrency10/adaptive), Tom primes KV cache and runs the 1k qps ramp, Liam produces batch histograms and a quick latency percentile chart, Maya will model price impact, we'll enable burst capacity for the controlled run (pin region), run duration 60 minutes each.
[06:36] Tom: i'll post results and top failure prompts to the pilot sheet and open a thread in the pilot slack.
[06:42] Liam: i'll attach the charts and the exact runtime flags we used.
[06:46] Maya: next sync friday same time, unless we need a 90-min deep dive earlier.
[06:52] Rachel: works for us. thanks all.
[06:55] (call end)

References/Links mentioned: pilot tracker (link), batch-distribution-chart (to be uploaded), SOC2+audit-log-integration.pdf (to be attached), pricing-impact-spreadsheet (to be shared)

Notes on transcript: some speaker labels were compressed; small transcription errors present (e.g., KV vs K-V, region names fuzzy).
